sections.heading: Overshoot from duty-cycle loss
sections.text: PSFB has inherent duty-cycle loss due to the leakage inductance commutation time. This reduces the effective duty cycle and requires a higher turns ratio. If overshoot occurs, verify the turns ratio accounts for duty-cycle loss. The voltage loop should be designed for the effective duty cycle, not the nominal.

sections.heading: Slow settling from ZVS loss
sections.text: If the PSFB loses ZVS (audible ringing on the primary), the switching losses increase and the effective gain changes. At light load, ZVS is lost — consider adaptive dead-time or burst mode. The current loop must handle the gain change from ZVS to hard-switching.

sections.heading: Excess ripple from secondary ringing
sections.text: The secondary rectifier ringing (from leakage inductance + junction capacitance) can couple to the output. Add RC snubbers across the secondary rectifiers. The output LC filter should be sized for the effective ripple frequency (2*fsw).

sections.heading: Efficiency from circulating current
sections.text: PSFB efficiency at light load suffers from circulating current in the primary leg during the freewheeling interval. The controller cannot fix this — it is a topology limitation. Consider burst mode or a different topology for high efficiency across the full load range.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the PSFB cannot meet specs across the full load range, consider: (1) LLC for fixed conversion ratio with wide ZVS, (2) full-bridge with active clamp for better ZVS, (3) DAB for bidirectional power flow.
